title: Cash, Cards and Electronic Payments
introduction: Explore cash, cards and electronic payments using everyday examples.
definition: Cash uses notes and coins. Debit cards and electronic wallets pay using available balances, while credit cards can create debt. Record payments, balances and change; do not assume that all payment methods have the same fees.

examples.question: An e-wallet has RM60. Pay RM23.50.

exercises.question: Cash RM50, purchase RM32. Change RM?
Debit account RM120, payment RM45. Balance RM?
E-wallet RM30, top up RM20. Balance RM?
RM100 credit purchase, repay RM40. Debt RM?
Three RM8 electronic payments total RM?
Does unpaid credit-card spending create debt? yes/no
exercises.solution: Yes. Credit-card spending uses borrowed money, which remains a debt until repaid.

summary: Cash uses notes and coins. Debit cards and electronic wallets pay using available balances, while credit cards can create debt. Record payments, balances and change; do not assume that all payment methods have the same fees.
